subject.title: fix(gateway): preserve abort after dispatch rejection

question: Should maintainers accept this focused Gateway terminal-precedence fix with the supplied Gateway/WebSocket proof, or require broader client/provider proof before merge?
rationale: The code path is a real bug fix with no concrete patch defect found, but it changes session-state and message-delivery precedence in a hot Gateway race path where green CI cannot prove every consumer expectation.

options.title: Land With Current Gateway Proof
options.body: Accept the focused regression tests, clean CI, and real Gateway/WebSocket proof as sufficient for this terminal-ordering repair.

options.title: Request Broader Client Proof
options.body: Ask for browser or native-client proof if maintainers want confidence in every consumer of the changed terminal states before merge.

options.title: Pause For Terminal Ownership Refactor
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want a centralized terminal-state ownership refactor before accepting another targeted race fix.

recommendation.title: Land With Current Gateway Proof
recommendation.body: Accept the focused regression tests, clean CI, and real Gateway/WebSocket proof as sufficient for this terminal-ordering repair.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main provenance points to recent Gateway chat ownership, and the decision is about accepting merge risk in that hot path.
